newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark welcomes world telecoms pact.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark welcomes world telecoms pact.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Monday it welcomed the weekend's global telecommunications pact, provided it was fair and equal for all companies and countries.

"In general we welcome every trend towards a liberalisation of telecommunications provided it is equal and fair and the same liberalisation for all countries and all companies," Tele Danmark spokesman Kim Ruberg told Reuters.
"We believe that liberalisation will help us to bring down international telephone call prices and enable us to negotiate better transit and termination prices," Ruberg said.

The World Trade Organisation (WTO) accord on telecommunications was signed by 68 countries on Saturday in Geneva after more than three years of on-off negotiations to bring free trade principles to the booming telecoms sector.
Ruberg said that he was confident that Tele Danmark was competitive and fully capable of taking advantage of the fully liberalised telecommunications market.
The Danish telecommunications market was liberalised in July 1996, with Tele Danmark, partially privatised in 1994 and 51.73 percent state-owned, the dominant operator.
